text:
Anya Patel: Heads up — saw a short spike from org:acme around 11:12 UTC, lasted ~20s and hit per-org throttle but not per-key. Noticed some 429s from preview users.
Matt Huang: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/preview/spikes?org=acme — looks like a dozen quick concurrent requests. Short, bursty. 
Sanjay Rao: Short spikes are expected. We should make a clearer distinction between burst credits and steady-state quota. Token bucket with a larger burst bucket for previews seems reasonable.
Kevin Li: Leaky-bucket smooths over bursts but increases latency for interactive flows. For previews I lean token-bucket with explicit credit accounting.
Lia Gomez: From console POV customers ask for a single toggle like "allow short bursts" not raw tokens. We should expose a human-friendly UX: e.g., "burst allowance: +X QPS for Y seconds".
Anya Patel: Proposed config (example):
```yaml
quota:
  sustained_qps: 5
  burst_capacity: 40  # tokens
  burst_window_s: 30  # window to consume burst
  refill_rate: 5
```
Matt Huang: Current impl: token-bucket is per-org and we have per-key fast path. Increasing burst_capacity for orgs risks noisy-neighbor effects if multiple keys consume it.
Sanjay Rao: Telemetry needed: add metrics burst_consumed_total, burst_debt, burst_replenish_rate with org_id label. Also track 429_by_reason (sustained vs burst).
Kevin Li: Operational safety: add absolute hard cap at infra level. Eg. max_tokens_per_sec_global = 2000 so one org can't exhaust cluster.
Lia Gomez: Console features to add: "burst credits remaining" as a numeric + estimated refill ETA, and a 1h heatmap of microbursts. This will help customers tune.
Anya Patel: Canary plan: feature-flag +2x burst_capacity for 10% of orgs (preview style) for 48h, run eval prompts and watch error/latency regressions.
Matt Huang: Also add alert rule: page if avg burst_debt > 50 for 5m or if cluster CPU > 85% while burst consumption > 10% of capacity.
Sanjay Rao: Quick perf tradeoffs: token-bucket gives us instantaneous allowance checks (O(1)). If we implement per-request durable accounting in redis we need to be careful with TTLs to avoid thundering. Example key: quota:org:{id}:tokens.
Kevin Li: Suggest fallback routing: when cluster load high, route burst requests to smaller/cheaper model or graceful degradation (truncate responses). That buys headroom.
Lia Gomez: I'll design the console layout: small summary banner + expandable panel with history. Will mock tomorrow and link. :memo:
Matt Huang: I'll add /quota/status?org={id} returning {sustained_qps, burst_remaining, refill_eta}. Keep it light.
Anya Patel: Starting canary flag roll now for 50 orgs (subset of the 10%). Will post results and metrics link.
OpsBot: quota-service v1.8.2 deploy started by @mhuang.
OpsBot: quota-service v1.8.2 deploy succeeded.
Matt Huang: Added metrics dashboards and the /quota/status endpoint in the canary cluster. Link: https://grafana.redwood/d/quota/canary-spike.
Sanjay Rao: Running e2e checks for race conditions in token refill. If anyone sees weird token inflation flag it here.
Kevin Li: If we see increased tail latency we should revert canary quickly. Keep revert playbook ready.
Lia Gomez: Ack — will push UX mock link in #design after lunch.
Anya Patel: Thanks all, will follow up with numbers in 24h. :eyes:
